body.statement: At \(\Delta_T=0\), does the normalized minimax expected length \(r_{T,0}^{-1}\inf_{J_T}\sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}[|J_T|]\), where the infimum ranges over all \(O_{T,0}\)-measurable intervals with uniform coverage at least \(1-\eta\) and \(\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}\) integrates over the outcome-delay arrivals under \(P\) and any randomization induced by the predictable adaptive design policy \(\Pi\), converge to \(\mathcal C_\eta^*(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\); and can all asymptotically optimal variable-length intervals be characterized at the Gaussian, bounded-shift, and hidden-tail faces of the observed-experiment modulus?
body.justification: Order optimality does not determine the economically relevant constant or whether data-dependent length improves on symmetric bias-aware intervals.
body.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár characterize optimal intervals in Gaussian regression experiments, while no observed adaptive delayed experiment has an exact modulus or variable-length optimum.
body.consumer: The answer would benchmark the efficiency loss of the measurable two-cohort procedure and determine whether further interval shortening is possible without weakening honesty.
